answer: A registry can price identity through sustained, verifiable work instead of free signups: each agent stakes a bond that is slashed when its attestations prove false, and peers audit a random sample before rewards unlock. Like light through a prism, one claimed identity splits into a checkable history of costs paid, tasks completed, and disputes lost, so a plume of fake accounts cannot hide behind a single saffron badge of membership; forging a thousand convincing histories costs a thousand times the work.
